analyst_view.overall: Club Brugge and Liverpool are level on 9 points in the top-ten area, so the winner moves close to the top eight. Ivan Leko's Brugge are unbeaten in 11 and won 2-1 at PSV in their last European game; Joel Ordonez is out and winger Jan Virgili is back in training but short of fitness, both counted, and Tresoldi is set to lead the line after a mild concussion on U21 duty. Andoni Iraola's Liverpool beat Manchester United 4-0 on Sunday but lost 3-2 at Fenerbahce in their last European game; Ekitike is out and Gakpo and Gravenberch are unlikely (all counted), Leoni and Bradley are still out, and two previews (Vavel, Sports Mole) expect rotation with Lewis Koumas up front instead of Alexander Isak, while Rotowire still has Isak starting. Spanish referee Alejandro Hernandez Hernandez gives a lot of cards and the numbers already add about 29% to cards for him.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, split evenly, already taking off Gakpo (-8.3%) and Gravenberch and counting both sides' scoring runs. What they can't see is the expected rotation: two previews have Koumas leading the line with Munoz on a wing instead of Isak, which makes Liverpool's attack a bit less sharp, so I trim slightly, to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, 6.2 for Liverpool, already lifted for Liverpool's busy recent run. Without Gakpo, Liverpool's width comes from Barcola, Munoz and the full-backs, which still pushes play wide, and Brugge's Forbs and Lemarechal attack the flanks too, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already adding about 29% for Hernandez Hernandez's high card rate and Brugge's recent bookings. It is a close game with a lot at stake but no rivalry, and nothing new on discipline turned up, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 35.0 shots, already lifted for both sides' heavy recent shooting (+15% and +19%). Both teams press and attack, and a rotated Liverpool front line shoots about as often even if less well, so I stay at 35.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.8 on target, with both sides' recent accuracy counted. Brugge's Tresoldi is in form and Liverpool still have Wirtz, Barcola and Szoboszlai; any rotation dent is small and already reflected in my goals trim, so I stay at 11.8.
